title: Add FP8/INT8 benchmark config schema + validation (model/GPU/runtime pins)
author: Rina Kobayashi
body:
Title: Add FP8/INT8 benchmark config schema + validation (model/GPU/runtime pins)

Context
As part of the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint we need a defensible, repeatable way to define experiment inputs that (a) pins the environment and runtime bits and (b) makes it hard to run a partially-specified or “quietly different” benchmark. Today our configs are informal YAML + ad-hoc flags; people are already diverging on GPU naming, runtime pin format, and quant mode naming.

This PR introduces a versioned benchmark configuration schema and a validator, plus sample configs and docs. This is intended to be the contract used by the matrix generator (next PR) and by perf-canary ingestion.

Summary of changes
1) New versioned config schema (v1)
- Adds a formal schema for a benchmark run config with explicit pins:
  - model: id/family/revision (string identifiers we already use in the harness)
  - quant: mode (fp16|fp8|int8) + optional profile name
  - runtime_pin: runtime git commit and build/container metadata
  - gpu: sku + count + optional MIG slice + clocks policy (documented)
  - environment_pin: driver/cuda/cudnn and OS image id (optional but strongly recommended)
  - workload: preset name (e.g. hosted_chat_prefill_heavy) OR inline workload definition
  - run: warmup, repetitions, seed, and artifact tags
- Adds schema_version: "v1" with strict unknown-field rejection to avoid “typo config” issues.

2) Validation tooling
- Adds `bench validate-config <path>`:
  - Parses YAML/JSON
  - Validates against the schema
  - Enforces additional invariants beyond structural schema:
    - runtime_pin must include at least one of {runtime_commit, runtime_image_digest}
    - gpu.sku must be one of the normalized SKUs (A100-80GB, H100-SXM, H200-SXM, L40S) (list is extendable)
    - quant.mode must be compatible with the requested workload (e.g. disallow fp8 with a workload that explicitly requires fp16 baseline-only)
    - when gpu.mig is set, gpu.count must be 1 (bench-lab limitation right now)
    - workload inline definitions must include prompt_distribution and decode_params

3) Sample configs + docs
- Adds sample configs under `configs/examples/quant/`:
  - llama3_1_70b_h100_fp8_streaming_chat.yaml
  - qwen2_5_72b_a100_int8_batch.yaml
  - mistral_large_h200_fp16_baseline.yaml
- Adds docs page describing:
  - required fields
  - how to pin runtime + environment
  - how we normalize GPU SKUs
  - recommended artifact tagging for downstream dashboards (model_family, quant_mode, gpu_sku, runtime_commit)

Design notes / decisions
- Schema format: implemented as Pydantic models (Python) with JSON Schema export, because the harness is Python-first and we want a single source of truth.
- GPU naming: normalized into a small canonical set to reduce tag cardinality and prevent A100 variants from being treated as separate SKUs by accident.
- Forward compatibility: schema_version gating + strict validation; we can add v2 later without breaking v1.
- We intentionally do not validate “model id exists in registry” here; that check belongs in the runner (networked) to keep `validate-config` fast/offline.

CLI usage
- Validate a config:
  - `bench validate-config configs/examples/quant/llama3_1_70b_h100_fp8_streaming_chat.yaml`
- Print JSON schema (useful for editors/CI):
  - `bench print-schema --version v1 > schema_v1.json`

Files / areas changed
- bench/config/schema_v1.py (new)
- bench/config/validators.py (new)
- bench/cli.py (adds validate-config and print-schema)
- configs/examples/quant/*.yaml (new examples)
- docs/config-schema.md (new)
- tests/test_config_validation.py (new)
- tests/data/invalid_configs/* (new)

Illustrative snippet (schema excerpt)
- `quant.mode`: enum ["fp16", "fp8", "int8"]
- `runtime_pin.runtime_commit`: regex `^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$`
- `gpu.sku`: enum ["A100-80GB", "H100-SXM", "H200-SXM", "L40S"]

Test plan
- Unit tests cover:
  - happy path example configs
  - unknown field rejection
  - invalid GPU SKU
  - missing runtime pin
  - MIG/count invariant
- Manually ran `bench validate-config` on all examples.

Rollout / follow-ups
- Next PR will wire this schema into the matrix generator and require validation in CI for configs checked into the repo.
- Once perf-canary starts consuming these configs, we can add an allowlist for experimental fields without relaxing strictness globally.

Review notes / conversation
- Claire Dubois: "Can we require clocks policy to be explicit so people don’t forget?"
  - Rina Kobayashi (author): Made clocks_policy optional but added a warning in docs and recommended default; enforcing it here would block current perf-lab runs where we don’t yet have consistent admin control across nodes.
- Noah Patel: "Normalize runtime pin naming: runtime_image_digest vs container_digest"
  - Updated to runtime_image_digest throughout + added backward-compatible alias parsing for old configs inside validate-config (deprecated warning only; no schema change).
- Isabella Rossi: "Please add invalid-config fixtures for common mistakes we’ve seen (typo quant=fp-8, missing schema_version)."
  - Added fixtures + tests.
- Sean Gallagher: "GPU SKU list should include the exact L40S string we use in provisioning tags; also document MIG limitation."
  - Updated enum to L40S and added explicit docs section on MIG.

CI / checks
- lint: pass
- unit tests: pass
- typecheck: pass
- docs build: pass

Merge
- Merged via squash to main.

Refs
- Linear: ENG-24810 (umbrella), ENG-24812 (reproducible perf-lab environment pinning)
- Sprint: FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint (benchmarking-and-perf-suite)
release_notes: Benchmark-lab: introduce versioned benchmark run config schema (v1) with CLI validation; add sample FP8/INT8 configs and documentation.
